margin_error_definition: Forecast error = predicted two-party D–R margin minus actual two-party D–R margin. Positive D+ means too Democratic; negative R+ means too Republican.
poll_miss_definition: Signed poll average error = the displayed historical poll-average two-party D–R margin minus actual two-party D–R margin. Positive D+ means the poll average leaned too Democratic; negative R+ means it leaned too Republican. House and Senate use exponential recency weighting across eligible archived polls with fieldwork ending on or before Election Day (60-day House and 7-day Senate half-lives). Governor uses the equal-weight mean of eligible polls ending in the final 30 days when available; otherwise it falls back to exponential recency weighting (30-day half-life). The error is unavailable only when no usable pre-election poll average exists.
poll_note: Historical House and Senate averages include all eligible archived polls ending by Election Day, with weights that halve every 60 days for House and every 7 days for Senate. Governor uses an equal-weight final-30-day average when available and otherwise a recency-weighted average with a 30-day half-life. Current 2026 poll values remain source-reported D–R margins in a simple unweighted average; no miss is calculated until the election occurs. First-public dates are not consistently recorded, so these archives do not establish which polls were publicly available before Election Day. error_sign_convention: Forecast error = predicted Democratic-minus-Republican margin minus actual Democratic-minus-Republican margin. Positive is D+ (too Democratic); negative is R+ (too Republican).
